title: Totentanz
text:
Totentanz

Club

A club. Pretty self-explanatory, right? Preem, 'cuz I don't feel like fucking explaining myself.
Totentanz is Maelstrom's den. We shred guitars, circuits and anything that looks too 'ganic, so don't be surprised if somebody cuts off your hand or something. It's no coincidence the club's name means the "Dance of Death." You come, you drink, you listen to music and shake some chrome. You either walk out, or you're carried out.

Concerts

Totentanz regularly organizes events for fans of hardcore music. We do battle-of-the-bands, jam sessions, 2020s-style chrome-core parties, etc. Our bar is stocked to the skull with booze and other custom Maelstrom substancezzzzz to get your rage on.
Safety 100% not guaranteed. They say it ain't happening at the Totentanz until twenty peeps hit the deck.

Concerts

The greatest of legends of rock and chrome metal have played here, including Balberith and Samurai. These days our regulars on the stage include Tainted Overlord and our own band, Tinnitus.
A word about Tinnitus. They only play at the Totentanz. Their most recognizable trait? Their members keep changing. Every dedicated Maelstromer's gotta prove themselves, talent or experience be damned. With Tinnitus, you'll never hear the same set. Shit, after a few concerts, you won't hear anything at all.

Contact

Questions, threats, complaints (if you fucking dare)? Send an email to:

totentanz@ncity.totentanz.web

They also love to go a little bit cuckoo on stage, so best to keep your distance if you don't want to be sliced into bite-size chunks! ... They've already taken over Asia, Australia and Europe... now they've set their sights on conquering America!

Purple Force! Red Menace! Blue Moon!

With their forces combined, Us Cracks' music is electrifying lazrpop fans around the world! Don't believe it? Go to one of their concerts and see for yourself! Mrau!

title: Petrochem
text:
Petrochem

Our mission.

Sustainable development.

Who we are

Services

Contact

Contact

Who are we?

Petrochem BetterLife is the world's largest producer of CHOOH2, the most ecologically-friendly consumer fuel – without it the world would stop dead in its tracks! CHOOH2 is a form of synthetic alcohol made from carefully selected, genetically modified wheat grain. The grain is sourced from our very own private landholdings, allowing us to ensure the highest possible quality at every stage in its production cycle. We also specialize in manufacturing fertilizer and pesticide and are the largest extractor of natural gas and oil. Petrochem – the world's favorite energy supplier.

Why "BetterLife?"

We want people to be happy and fulfilled in their lives. That's why we conduct cutting-edge research to invent increasingly more effective energy resources, while also promoting various philanthropic causes. We help gifted young people from impoverished families achieve their full potential so that they can succeed in the world of science and technology.

Our mission.

Sustainable development.

Welcome to my Samurai netpage. If you know, you know. If you don't, then you don't know fuck-all. SILVERHAND 4 LIFE!!!
Karim_012

The greatest band of all time was formed at the start of the 21st century in Night City. Its members included:

·   Johnny Silverhand – the lord of punk, anti-establishment warrior, ex-soldier and arch-nemesis of corporations. Vocals/guitar.
·   Kerry Eurodyne – a pal of Johnny's who sang almost just as good, but without that extra edge. He went mainstream after the band split up. Vocals/guitar.
·   Denny – a tough-as-nails chick who beat the shit out of those drums. Drums.
·   Nancy (currently known as Bes Isis) – a virtuoso on the keys. Apparently she threw her abusive husband out of a megablock window. Too bad she sold out to N54 News. Keyboard.
·   Henry – a do-it-all whiz kid. Worked on the first personal link prototype.

Samurai started out by playing in a small, smoke-filled club called the Rainbow Cadenza. I'll never forget the vibe. Dust-ups with corpos, drinking contests with Nance, listening to Johnny's hour-long tirades... not to mention his sense of humor. One time he printed shirts for a 2020 worldwide concert tour - it's funny because Samurai couldn't even get an arena gig in the states. He picked some really random places... Beijing, Sapporo, Katowice. Happen to have one of the shirts myself. Too bad no one got the joke.
Real rock with a capital R died the way of Silverhand – with a flash and tower-crumbling bang.
We're still here listening to your songs, Johnny. And we remember. There's nothing left for us.

title: Denya Jinja Shrine
text:
Denya Jinja Shrine

The first shintō shrine in Night City. The Denya-Jinja pavilion is dedicated to the kami of chrome, night and electricity. Here you shall restore your vital energy, drawing strength from ancient Japanese traditions fused with the elements of modernity. Created from the synthesis of metal and neon, Denya-Jinja is the perfect place to find inner harmony in an age of chrome.
On the pavilion grounds you can supply yourself with maneki neko and omamori amulets, as well as stamp your goshuincho. For an additional charge, our monks also perform rituals to ward of evil spirits, bless construction sites for homes and businesses, and officiate wedding ceremonies.

Vending machines stocked with food and drinks are also available on the shrine grounds.

Please note! All tourists wishing to enter the shrine must purchase a ticket.

title: NETdir://traumateam.corp/inside
text:
Trauma Team: Behind the Scenes

We want YOU!

Log Out

When The Biomon Goes Quiet – A Paramedic's Story

Age of Wisdom – A Security Expert's Story

In the Line of Fire – A Pilot's Story

My last call? Yesterday, just after midnight, an accident was reported outside the Dark Matter club involving one of our clients. His biomonitor readings went completely haywire - it was impossible to decipher while en route. Once we'd arrived, we realized this wasn't an accident at all.

The client's Caliburn was engulfed in flames - scans indicated it was caused by a grenade launcher. The client's body lay a few feet away, with second-degree burns and a trail of blood leading back to the burning wreck he had crawled out of. His left hand was missing, blown off during the blast. That's why his biomonitor's data was all over the place. We detected no armed individuals in the vicinity. Inside the Caliburn were a woman's remains reduced to charred bone. No Trauma Team insurance. We evacced our client and managed to stabilize him en route to the hospital. He made it.

The next day, we gleaned the rest of the story from the screamsheets. Our patient was a well-known agent for BD stars. It was an assassination attempt. And thanks to us, he survived.

On every call I have a single task - ensure the complete safety of our patients and crew on board. Sometimes a call that seems at first like a normal, routine pickup turns into a living nightmare.

For instance, we were called by a patient, an elderly woman, who uses a wheelchair. It was the chair's readings that alerted us - the woman was suffocating due to a malfunctioning tracheal implant. The second we landed on her property in North Oak, we realized it was much worse - broken windows, house alarm switched off. Someone jammed the localNet. Inside it was even more dire - the corpses of our client's employees, including the gardener, cook, the nurses. The assailants were still inside when we reached them. Once they were neutralized, our paramedics tried to locate the patient while I secured the premises. Seven attackers in total. I couldn't tell if they were gangoons, mercenaries, or ordinary burglars. What I did know is that every house like this had a panic room. We found it in the basement behind a movable wall.

Our patient was inside, barely alive, her breathing shallow, probably thinking that she'd made it here for nothing. She was the one who had damaged her implant knowing it would alert us. She survived. A clever lady. She ended up moving away from Night City.

Piloting an AV in a place like Night City is a challenge in and of itself. We rarely land on megatower rooftops or wide, comfortable intersections. Those kinds of calls are relatively rare, or rather other units answer them instead of us. We land in the weirdest locations - under bridges, squeezing ourselves on cramped megablock balconies, in dark, narrow alleyways and sometimes even inside buildings when a gas leak blows out nearly the entire wall on the ninth floor of an office 'scraper. But the real fun starts when we need to land under fire.

Take just last month. We receive a call - two injured from gunfire, luckily the lead went clean through. When we got there, it turned out we had to land between two gangs duking it out. Our client was some big shot for one of the sides. We didn't have a choice - to secure the patient, we had to enter the fray.

You can guess what happened next. Our patient's gang celebrated that day. And our client? He was smiling all the way to the hospital. To this day I still wonder if it wasn't his own chooms who shot him. To get even.

Laurie Zamora

Tyler Brock

Luisa Jacobson

You're here because you want to join the largest medical corporation on the planet. You want to become one of us - an expert who helps patients and never abandons them in their hour of need, no matter the circumstances. That's why we're different. We're brave. We get it done. We're Trauma Team.

During the first step of your internship, you'll learn about all of our activities, from administration to technical support, equipment and weapons all the way to our elite, highly-specialized teams of paramedics, med-techies, security specialists and pilots. Our units arrive at the scene no more than seven minutes after receiving a distress signal and frequently land on difficult terrain or under fire. Hungry for some action? title: Vote for Peralez!
text:
Vote for Peralez!

Official campaign site

Campaign

Events

Get to know me

How can you help?

I've always been an activist for social change. That's why I'm running for mayor of Night City, because I know what the people of this city need. I know because I'm one of them. Under the neat haircut and clean suit, I'm just a kid who grew up on the streets of Heywood. If anyone knows how hard it is to break out of the vicious cycle of poverty, it's me.

Thanks to the Night Foundation Scholarship, I had the privilege of studying at the Asukaga university in Berkeley. Out of thirty candidates, only five received full funding. I'm not saying this to brag, but because to this very day I think about all those who weren't so fortunate, about the millions who didn't get the same chance I did. Deep inside, I know I owe something to them – them and their children, who face the same barriers their parents did a generation ago.

In terms of the injustices facing us today, the runner-up to social immobility is corruption. We've put up with city council and NCPD palm-greasing for far too long. Something has to be done. Something CAN be done. That's why I'm refusing support – financial or otherwise – from any large corporations. Only a mayor that's fully independent can bring about real change in this city, and together we can make that happen.

title: Night City Center for Psychiatric Health
text:
Night City Center for Psychiatric Health

Looking for help? At your rope's end? Is there a feeling buried deep inside you that doesn't belong there?

Our clinic was founded to support those who need a break from the anxieties and worries of daily existence. We help anyone and everyone, regardless of whether they have minor depression or suicidal thoughts. Thanks to the groundbreaking therapy program, "Safe Space," and the world-class care offered by our specialists, by the time patients check out of our facilities, they're able to seamlessly re-adapt to the real world and seize the day.
Our treatment methods include classical psychiatry, individual and group psychotherapy, as well as electrotherapy. Beyond our healthcare and rehabilitation departments, we also pride ourselves on our state-of-the-art cyberpsychological facility equipped with specialized equipment designed to disassemble the mind, as well as psychosurgery and braindance conditioning.

Please note that out of concern for the comfort and safety of our patients, the NC Center for Psychiatric Health do not permit visiting hours. In order for our treatments to yield results, patients must be completely isolated from external negative stimuli.
Thank you for your understanding.

title: NETdir://orbitalair.corp
text:
About

Services

A PIONEER OF SPACE EXPLORATION
Orbital Air was founded in Nairobi, Kenya at the start of the 21st century. We're the oldest and largest corporation serving passengers and cargo transport into near-Earth orbit.
We are the stewards of the majority of planetside spaceports, the crown jewel of which is located in Mogadishu, Somalia.
Our cutting-edge Orbital Air fleet consists of heavy-lift launch vehicles, manned and unmanned spacecraft as well as 300 commercial shuttles. Our rockets such as the Hermes were the first space ships to be sent to space by the European Space Council.

A TITAN OF TRANSPORT
Besides the orbital transport of people and goods, Orbital Air offers a variety of services including construction and maintenance of orbital stations as well as satellite networks. We also maintain rocketless launchpads using electromagnetic catapults, more commonly known as mass drivers. Thanks to all this, we've greatly reduced the cost of cargo transport into low-Earth orbit and have established a strong foothold in the space exploration industry.

A LEADER OF INNOVATION
We're proud that Orbital Air remains the uncontested leader in the field of orbital tech innovation. Since the beginning of our company, we've invested tremendous resources into exploration and space colonization. In cooperation with the leaders of New Africa, we're continuing our research into the Alpha Centauri system. An unmanned space probe equipped with an advanced AI has set off for the planet Proxima Centauri b, the closest Earth-type extrasolar planet to us, 40 trillion kilometers (4 light years) away. The probe is expected to land in 2095.

title: NETdir://orbitalair.corp/travel
text:
About

Services

Traveling with Orbital Air

NCX

OA Black

Uncover the mysteries of outer space on board Orbital Air's OA Black spaceplane. Our newest fleet of space voyagers are now open for business! All you need to do is provide us with your coordinates and a private charter shuttle will take you far above Earth's orbit. The purpose of your flight will be kept a secret to everyone except for the crew and pilot who will ensure you have a comfortable, relaxing experience.

Find out more about chartering a spaceplane by booking an appointment with an Orbital Air representative at a time and place that is convenient for you.

Crystal Palace Direct

Welcome to the kingdom of relaxation, luxury and entertainment - Crystal Palace! The five-level space station was purpose-built to provide you with countless attractions and best of all - with OA Crystal Palace Direct orbital shuttles you can get there without a layover at the moon!
Disembarking at Crystal Palace is preceded by an automated shuttle transfer of the passenger pod to an Aldrin Cycler docking module, which is carried out in low Earth orbit. Reserve your stay in an apartment with a panoramic view of the Earth and let us do the rest!

IMPORTANT ANNOUNCEMENT! Due to the growing number of travelers stranded with casino-related debts, travelers are obliged to show their return ticket back to Earth PRIOR to boarding a shuttle bound for Crystal Palace.

OA HighLines

Traveling on the luxury OA HighLines space shuttle is the perfect solution for someone who values quality service and a high standard of comfort.

What to visit? Choose from among 80 terrestrial destinations available on board or charter a space shuttle for a private flight at your convenience.

Your unique experiences with OA HighLines begin before you even board - passengers are entitled to the use of exclusive private all-inclusive lounges to relax before their flight. Once on board our space shuttle, you can recline back in your seat while enjoying an in-flight meal and entertainment system. It's only a shame that the flight from Johannesburg to Atlanta takes... only 33 minutes!

Can't fly? That's what Orbital Air is for!
Introducing our newest fleet of orbital spaceplanes with over 80 destinations to choose from around the globe - and that's not all! Fly with one of our five flight services, whether you're on a tight budget or want an exclusive charter, with Orbital Air you'll reach your destination quickly and safely - both on and off planet!

OA TerraLines

A well-deserved vacation, business trip, or maybe a one-way ticket? With Orbital Air's spaceplanes, you can go anywhere - quickly, comfortably and for affordable prices!

Why travel aboard normal airplanes when OA Terralines can take you from Night City to Sidney in just a single hour! So what are you waiting for? Check out more than 80 available flights and reserve your ticket today.

OA TychoLines

Tycho is a bustling city on Luna that is attracting a growing number of tourists, corporate employees and orbital migrants. No matter what category you fall into, OA TychoLines will get you safely to the moon in just 16 hours!

Before traveling we advise that you familiarize yourself with the flight handbook, where you'll find useful tips about luggage types and sizes as well as medical requirements that are mandatory for all passengers traveling to Low Earth Orbit.

IMPORTANT ANNOUNCEMENT! Due to the ongoing modernization of Tycho Terminal (Terminal B) at NCX, all flights to Tycho have been suspended until further notice. To book a ticket for another Orbital Air spaceport, please contact Customer Service.

title: North America's largest spaceport
text:
About

Services

Traveling with Orbital Air

NCX

North America's largest spaceport

A state-of-the-art spaceport that offers more than 80 destinations around the globe and beyond.
Five airlines offering different prices and levels of comfort to match the needs of every passenger.
A fleet of cutting-edge, reliable air and spacecrafts that will quickly and safely reach any destination.
Book your ticket on with NCX and enjoy unrivalled quality service guaranteed by Orbital Air.

Terminal Tycho Modernization

To ensure the comfort and safety of our passengers and to answer the growing demand for OA Tycho spacelines, NCX management has decided to embark on a comprehensive modernization of Tycho Terminal (Terminal B), including the reconstruction and expansion of the terminal and launchpads. As Kojo Kariuki (OA Senior Manager of North American Developments) said, this undertaking will expand the terminal's capacity to 1300 departing and 1300 arriving travelers every hour.

A larger and updated Terminal Tycho will also allow quicker and more efficient passenger service and expand the number of flights - including cargo transports that will supply Tycho residents with essential goods. It will also become possible to transport parcels that require special storage conditions, such as radioactive materials.

The contractor of Tycho Terminal's modernization for design and construction is Night City's very own Corp-Bud. The opening date of the new Tycho Terminal remains under negotiation.

NCX Terrorist Attack

The terrorist attack on Night City International and Translunar is a barbaric and unprecedented violation of international law, but most of all a human tragedy that brutally took innocent lives and left families in mourning.

Orbital Air has pledged to continue its investigation in identifying the organizers of the attack and bringing them to justice.

At the same time, Orbital Air has made clear that no act of violence will hinder the peaceful exploration of space exploration, which according to the Outer Space Treaty is the domain of all mankind.

Orbital Air offers its deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims. Those traveling or visiting NCX may privately express their grief via the condolence message board located near Terminal B.

title: We want Night City in the NUSA!

We want Night City in the NUSA!

We demand the return of Night City to the New United States of America!

We're fed up living in constant fear! Stop the chaos and lawlessness on the streets of our homeland! Gangers, petty criminals, cyberpsychos and hostile foreign agents run amok in Night City! They steal from us, murder, destroy property and the NCPD doesn't lift a finger! Is this what a healthy, neopostmodernist society is supposed to look like? Is this our city of dreams?

The facts speak for themselves: crime in the NUSA is two times lower than in Night City. Unfortunately, it's all too clear that the authorities are incapable of ensuring the public's safety. They lack the means that only a strong, large, smoothly functioning government can provide. Acceding to the New United States of America would provide much-needed municipal aid, new jobs and even greater access to better, cheaper implants.
We can do better! Let's join the NUSA!

The Mayor of Night City oversees the Treasurer's Office, the deputies to the mayor and directs the heads of the city's departments, including Night City Police Department.

Night City's system of governance is based on the authority of the mayor in cooperation with the Night City Council, whose members are elected along neodemocratic lines by the ten largest corporations headquartered in Night city.

The Mayor of Night City is the city's highest governing representative. He or she has the power to appoint department heads and commissioners as well as remove public officials from office. Part of the mayor's proposals are subject to approval from the Night City Council.

With every new mayor comes an office with new faces.

LUCIUS RHYNE
Mayor of Night City
Lucius Rhyne was born on October 12th in 2017 in a Trauma Team clinic in Night City. His father worked at Arasaka, while his mother was a NetWatch officer. His childhood was eclipsed by the 4th Corporate War and its tragic effects – his father was killed in the Arasaka Headquarters Bombing of 2023. Growing up in the shadow of immeasurable devastation, Rhyne made a lifelong commitment to fight for peace and order.

Only a few years later, cruel fate struck once again – Rhyne's mother was captured by one of Bartmoss's rogue AI while on a mission in cyberspace. In spite of the financial hardship of providing care for his mother's body, Rhyne enrolled at the Richard Night University and graduated in Cybernetic Law. He embarked on a professional career for 20 years before he became a member of the Night City Council.

Rhyne's greatest achievements include passing resolutions on neuro-cognitive implants as well as defending Night City from the NUSA's siege during the Metal Wars. Thanks to his judgment and strength of character, Arasaka was able to return to Night City after more than four decades of absence, after which Militech forces retreated from the Coronado Bay and the metropolis retained its independence. Shortly thereafter, Lucius Rhyne was elected as the mayor of Night City and holds his position until today.

JEFFERSON PERALEZ

Jefferson Peralez was born on July 4th, 2031 in Night City. His parents owned a small restaurant in Heywood. Despite a family of small means, Peralez claims he had a happy childhood, and the district he grew up in still retains a special place in his heart. Thanks to the support of his family and his innate determination, Peralez graduate from high school at the top of his class and enrolled in the Asukaga University in Berkeley with the help of a scholarship from the Richard Night Foundation. He was the fastest student ever to be awarded a doctorate. One of the scholarship's other recipients was Elizabeth, who would later become his wife.

After leaving college, Peralez worked for several years at the renowned Asukaga & Finch law firm while also becoming increasingly engaged in Night City's civic life. He soon became the Assistant Attorney General of Night City, before soon assuming the role Attorney General. In the last few months, Peralez has been a member of the Night City Council, using his influence to campaign against corruption and improve the basic living standards of Night City's most disadvantaged citizens.

Mayor of Night City since 2077.

title: Weldon Holt
text:
Weldon Holt

Worthy replacement? Holt is a CLONE of Lucius Rhyne!

If you're all still wondering what really happened to the late mayor of Night City, Lucius Rhyne, then look no further. Before his death, Rhyne was cloned and his appearance changed with the help of plastic surgery. Wondering what he looks like now? Ladies and gentlemen, I give you his replacement, Weldon Holt! No doubt, Rhyne has come up with an ingenious way of holding on to power in perpetuity.

SPOTTED in the Caymans! Lucius Rhyne is alive and kicking!

The late Lucius Rhyne, whose untimely death shook Night City to its core, is in fact alive and well! He was seen recently in the Cayman Islands, sipping a piña colada on the beach.
Weldon Holt, who replaced Rhyne and is running for reelection, declined to comment. This simply proves that not only was Holt aware of Rhyne, he presumably aided him in going incognito.

Holt SOLD Night City to Arasaka! "They gave the most."

Weldon Holt, candidate for Night City's upcoming mayoral elections, was overheard talking on the holo with his campaign manager about campaign finance contributions when he said the words, "Arasaka gave the most." Now we know who'll be REALLY calling the shots in this city for the next four years.

The SHOCKING TRUTH about Rhyne's death! Holt is GUILTY!

According to official reports, three months ago the mayor of Night City, Lucius Rhyne, suffered a massive heart attack. But the facts paint a darker picture. Sources close to the NCPD claim that none other than Rhyne's replacement and current mayor of Night City, Weldon Holt, is responsible for his death. The NCPD has yet to make an official announcement and Holt continues to decline to comment on the matter.

Dealing with SCAVS! Weldon Holt CAUGHT selling human organs!

On his official site, the candidate for the mayor of Night City is urging Night Citizens to help finance his campaign. He must be really desperate if he's had to resort to trading human organs. Holt was recently spotted engaging in commerce with individuals closely tied to scavengers, and everyone knows what the scavengers deal in.

Arch Nazaré

The Arch Nazaré is a unique mix between a cruiser and a racing bike – like an outcast, it refuses strict labels. Equipped with a single-sided, aluminium swingarm and cutting-edge steering capabilities, the Nazaré is perfect for an aggressive riding style. The true meat of this motorcycle is in the engine, complete with a ventilation system designed by our very own engineers.

Arch Substance 171 (COMING SOON!)

The Arch Substance 171 was built with one aim in mind – to achieve the impossible. Crafted from an intricate blend of carbon fiber, aluminum and cured leather, the Arch Substance 171 rests on an ultralight, nanocellular frame, giving it an agility and manoeuvrability that – powered by a CHOOH2-combustible engine – allows it to reach speeds never before imagined.

What is Arch?

When passion meets inspiration, an obsession is born.

Arch Motorcycle is modernity at its essence. Since 2011 our aim is to provide our customers with an unrivaled cruising experience thanks to our innovative designs and engineering perfection. Every Arch motorcycle is custom-made to order and tailored to its owner's highest expectations.

Arch Motorcycle is strength in moderation. We work tirelessly to find the simplest solutions to maximize our motorcycles' performance. We carefully select each and every component, from the sleek, practical body down to the axle.

Arch Motorcycle is about fine tuning the little details. In the age of automated mass-production, we still believe that a motorcycle with soul can only be crafted by hand. All of our motorcycles are built from start-to-finish by a single engineer, guaranteeing the highest level of quality and precision for every Arch.

Arch is coming to Night City!

It is our pleasure to announce that Arch Motorcycle will soon be opening a new dealership in Night City! Ready-made motorcycles will be available on site, as well as the opportunity to customize the bike of your dreams.

More details coming soon.

title: Night City
text:
Night City

Who we are

Who we are

[CUT CANDIDATE]

Announcements

Safe 'n' Sound

In recent years the NCPD (Night City Police Department) has been the subject of various rumors. Out of concern for your trust and safety, we have decided to cut through the chaos of misinformation and dispel some of the most widely-circulated claims about us.

Three questions about the NCPD

1. Q: Will NCPD officers protect me in all areas of Night City?
A: Sadly, no. The NCPD can only ensure the safety of Night Citizens in districts such as City Center or North Oak. Areas such as Pacifica and Dogtown do not fall under our jurisdiction. It's also worth remembering that the NCPD does not patrol corporate territories, or any territory outside of Night City limits.

2. Q: Is the NCPD funded by corporations?
A: No. The NCPD receives funding directly from the Office of the Mayor and the City Council. Corporations have no influence on us. Relying on their financial resources would be akin to corruption, which is something we would obviously want to avoid. Our officers are not as well equipped as their corporate counterparts, but they more than make up for it with their moral compass and sense of public duty.

3. Q: Do officers in the MaxTac unit take civilians and their lives into account?
A: Yes. The idea that MaxTac officers aim to neutralize cyberpsychos at all costs is a blatant falsehood. Their priority is to minimize damage and loss of human life. Unfortunately, accidents sometimes occur, and for that we deeply apologize.

MaxTac celebrates another victory! Officers fatally shot a cyberpsycho who attempted to break into a WNS studio. Four Arroyo residents have been arrested after throwing rotten syn-meat at a Cytech delivery truck. The attackers, found to be intoxicated upon their arrest, are facing up to five years behind bars.

The battle against piracy rages on

Drunks in Arroyo apprehended

Suicide rate on the decline

According to the most recent statistical analyses, the suicide rate among police officers in Night City has declined by 0.5%. Sociologists credit the results to a new officer mental health program which uses negative thought-suppressing braindances. Go NCPD!

Dangerous driver arrested!

Night City police have arrested a driver who opened fire on another road user. Officers restrained and arrested the shooter and subjected him to a psychological evaluation. After cyberpsychosis was ruled out, the man was cautioned and given a fine of €$1000.

The world has changed, but the devil as not.
Darkness is blinding the eyes of humankind. We have adapted our flesh and blood to cyberware, computers and strings of code. They can take out my transmitters and jam my frequencies, but I'll always find a way to bounce back! If you're a nuisance, that means you're doing something right. 'Cause as you know, nothing here is taboo - this is a space to talk about anything, anyone, any-goddamn-time. If something's important for you, then it's important for me! Let's parley over the air, wire it up, spin it hard. If you don't talk about it, does it even exist? So let's amp things up and make some noise on the air! I growl, you roar!

I heard about a lot of issues that Julio ran into when he wanted open a stall selling coxinhas. I know it's not easy for folks to start a business in Dogtown, but in Julio's case, Barghest really crossed the line. Which is why, my chooms, we're throwing a FUNDRAISER! Julio promises a coxinha for every eurobuck thrown into our piggy bank! Let's help a choom out and show those yellow-painted assholes that we don't scare easy.

If you make your own music and want folks to listen to it - I'm your guy! You send me your songs and I'll spin 'em on Growl FM. Just remember - your music's going straight into our earholes and peeps'll have opinions, so have your tearbucket ready. But hey, least they're talkin' about it, right?

Chrome_Squirrel

06-12-2077

OK, so about the recent broadcast: yes, social injustice is the biggest killer in the world INCLUDING in Night City. Just recently I was digging through some sociological studies comparing the average person's life in Watson and Pacifica with Westbrook. Did you know those one percenters live almost 18 years longer than us ordinary peeps?! Money's the main reason, of course - I can't afford the most expensive docs (ripper or otherwise) or the best chrome. But that's not all - I'll bet in Westbrook they're not working 14-hour days in stuffy warehouses and eat powdered scop, meanwhile their shoe cabinets are bigger than our entire units, most of which are taken up by our old, shitty feeders. So yeah...

GlidElf#Adam

06-06-2077

Hi there, I work in small clinic on the outskirts of Pacifica. It's just one doc and one ripper. We don't advertise because we can't afford it, we're not insured because our patients can't afford insurance either. Still, every day we get so many folks that we have to send them to other places like that infirmary at the church in Dogtown (and yes, everything you've heard about Dogtown is true, so just imagine how desperate we are). Our patients are sick, exhausted, without hope. In the eyes of the city's leaders, they don't exist. Plugging them into the some kind of social safety net - I'm talking basic health care or food support - would sully their statistics and pull them into even more debt. So best to turn the other cheek. Except they exist, they're here living and dying on the margins. And people like me or my colleague at the clinic...? We'll die right beside them. Not from overwork, no, but for lack of better possibilities...

Br41n_34ter

04-23-2077

Growl FM Hotline

Contact us

Everyone here keeps yakking away about their living conditions, work-life balance, but I think the main result of all this injustice is simply the state of fuckedupness that people like you and me fall into. Fuckedupness is what makes your breathing and thinking shallow because everything else has been taken by those at the top. Some say it's "God", others that it's the corpos in their glass towers. Same shit. We're fucked and we're never gonna unfuck ourselves while this city's enormous boot pushes through this meatgrinder we call a life (because we're fucked). You punch out from work before the sun comes up but you don't give a damn if it's night or day because it's always just fucking dark. You go to the vending machine and it starts spouting ads and feel-good motivational bullshit and you just want a Broseph to help you fall asleep while praying to God the neighbors don't wake you up with their shouting who the fuck knows why probably because they don't have money, love or even really each other. Then the radio wakes you up with an upbeat "Goooooood morning, Night City!" like it's the best fucking news you've heard in your life. No, good news would be if I actually saw the light at the end of this tunnel of fuckedupness. But I won't because I already said for people like you and me Night City is only and always dark.

Coeur Noir

Coeur Noir is a French duo who left Neo-Montpellier for Night City to find their lost drummer. Who doesn't like a good hero story? But we've all been there and know how this tale unfolded. Night City sucked them in like the neon-drenched venus flytrap it is.

When walking the dark alleyways of Santo Domingo, Paka (vocalist, composer) and Jod (guitarist, composer) got jumped and lost everything they had on them, including their digital identities. The nearest embassy – SoCal. Yeesh... So, now, the two have only a handful of pocket lint to their names and still no sign of their long-lost percussionist. Honest talk though, NC  just isn't the place where heroes are born. Word is they've hired a Mox netrunner to help get them back on their feet, but data recovery on this scale doesn't come cheap. If you'd like to do your part to help, keep an eye out for gig posters. If they're putting on a show, the least you could do is toss an enny their way by buying a ticket.

And you, mystery drummer, if you're reading this, the time has come to reveal yourself. The guys are staying in Heywood. Said it reminds them of European cities somehow. Wouldn't know how, exactly, never been. But I take their word for it! Hope y'all can finally meet up.

In the meantime, I hope everyone else has a chance to take a ride on our airwaves for a listen to "Let The Stars Die". What. A. Track! Like a delicious cry made of equal parts anger and sadness, spritzed with confusion and dissociation, then poured into a tall glass of infinite void. Does that make sense? Whatever. Life is fucking complicated. If one of you, dear listeners, can dig deeper beneath the surface, hit me up and let me know what you find. But what I don't understand, I can FEEL in this track. Shivers, chills, goosebumps – you name it, I got it.

Finally, I have a message to pass along from Coeur Noir to their fans:

"Never forget to love."

P.S. One final tip from me - watch out for that new gen of neuroviruses floating around. It'll do a number on your digital ID data, royally fucking up any and all bio-authorization services you might be using.

Red Dead Roadkill

Dunno know if you peeps believe in something as warm 'n' fuzzy as destiny while we hurtle through the infinite void on this tiny, blue orb, but the origin story of Red Dead Roadkill feels like just that – destiny. Following a family tragedy caused by a defective black market implant, Bob (guitarist, backing vocalist) joined up with Folk Nation out in the Badlands. All he had to his name was his tormented past, a new family of circumstance and a guitar. But during a psyche-cleansing ritual (which involved a nasty trip on Blue Glass), he had a vision of a woman singing – a woman with hair of fire. Holy shit if that isn't poetic, right?

Spoilers: Bob found the woman. Obviously. Otherwise I wouldn't be here telling the story. That said, it wasn't easy. He searched far and wide, traveling from city to city, until he found Dee (vocalist, percussionist) singing by a campfire in a nomad camp somewhere in the Badlands. The two of them clicked instantly, especially musically. Another point to all you peeps out there who believe in destiny. It wasn't long before they assembled a couple of their chooms to fill out the rest of the band: Saibot (bassist) and Cole (drummer). Thus Roadkill was born.

Things were going well. But, as with any band with an upward trajectory, the higher they climbed, the more drama they encountered. The money was... liveable, the tours – exhausting and chaotic. What's more, their manager—Dee's boyfriend—had a murky gangoon past (and present, as it later turned out). And then there was the crash involving the band's tour bus, after which nothing was ever the same – especially for Cole.

So, what's a band to do after such a string of unfortunate events? They had two options: go their separate ways, or forge the band into something new. Forge they did. Red Dead Roadkill survived the ups and downs and eventually got back to the music, though now with a slightly different lineup. Saibot left the band and was replaced by Sub on the bass, who plays their gigs remotely as a holo-projection. But hot damn! Whoever said you need physical presence to have STAGE PRESENCE?!

Tune in to Growl's airwaves for a listen to "Flatline". This track offers is a glimpse into the depths of human connecton and true loss. It draws from raw emotion, courage, and above all, the realization of our own fragility as we walk the path to self-destruction. The song also draws inspiration from the band's beginnings by using the final heartbeats of Bob's dying father. Hardcore, chooms. Hard. Core.

Now, a message from the band:

"There's always something left to say,
Needless things to say anyway.
Still I hold on to yesterday,
Though it’s wrong I recognize."

Following a family tragedy caused by a defective black market implant, Bob (guitarist, backing vocalist) joined up with Folk Nation out in the Badlands. All he had to his name was his tormented past, a new family of circumstance and a guitar. But during a psyche-cleansing ritual (which involved a nasty trip on Blue Glass), he had a vision of a woman singing – a woman with hair of fire. Holy shit if that isn't poetic, right?

Spoilers: Bob found the woman. Obviously. Otherwise I wouldn't be here telling the story. That said, it wasn't easy. He searched far and wide, traveling from city to city, until he found Dee (vocalist, percussionist) singing by a campfire in a nomad camp somewhere in the Badlands. The two of them clicked instantly, especially musically. Another point to all you peeps out there who believe in destiny. It wasn't long before they assembled a couple of their chooms to fill out the rest of the band: Saibot (bassist) and Cole (drummer). Thus Roadkill was born.

Things were going well. But, as with any band with an upward trajectory, the higher they climbed, the more drama they encountered. The money was... liveable, the tours – exhausting and chaotic. What's more, their manager—Dee's boyfriend—had a murky gangoon past (and present, as it later turned out). And then there was the crash involving the band's tour bus, after which nothing was ever the same – especially for Cole.

So, what's a band to do after such a string of unfortunate events? They had two options: go their separate ways, or forge the band into something new. Forge they did. Red Dead Roadkill survived the ups and downs and eventually got back to the music, though now with a slightly different lineup. Saibot left the band and was replaced by Sub on the bass, who plays their gigs remotely as a holo-projection. But hot damn! Whoever said you need physical presence to have STAGE PRESENCE?!

Tune in to Growl's airwaves for a listen to "Flatline". This track offers is a glimpse into the depths of human connecton and true loss. It draws from raw emotion, courage, and above all, the realization of our own fragility as we walk the path to self-destruction. The song also draws inspiration from the band's beginnings by using the final heartbeats of Bob's dying father. Hardcore, chooms. Hard. Core.

Now, a message from the band:

"There's always something left to say,
Needless things to say anyway.
Still I hold on to yesterday,
Though it’s wrong I recognize."

text:

Hotline

Spirit Machines

This four-piece band is a Molotov cocktail with 3/4 raw, unfiltered Night City laced with 1/4 Nomad motor oil. When he's not scraping his ax, Dave Crespo (guitars), who might actually be the biological son of Dino Dinovic (Dino, if you're reading this, fess up!!), also runs podcasts and DJs - a true renaissance man for our time.

Pepper Rose (vocals, lyrics) comes from refined, blue-blooded corpo stock... that is until she was disinherited. For a while she worked in Trauma Team before they got rid of her too (apparently her baggage is of the illegal variety...?). On top of that, I've heard she's a decent chemist and tarot card reader. Could it be worth combining both of those talents - cards and fumes - for a life-changing (or life-ending) reading? Absolutely.

Michael Collins (percussion) is a known quantity in the corpo world, taking on contracts and negotatiating deals - his speciality apparently lies in hostile takeovers and rocky mergers. That might explain his nerves of steel and mind-bending improv skills - a virtuoso at everything he touches.

Then there's Sergio (with that undulating bass!) from the Thelas Nation, owner of the band's bulletproof tour van that's beefed up like a goddamned tank. He's undoubtedly responsible for that "wide open road" undercurrent coursing through the band's hard rock sound that makes you want to drive straight into the sunset.

Their hit single "Candy Shell" gets your foot tapping, your heart racing and your entire being itching to seize something - the day, the moment, whatever'll jumpstart that change you need in life. It'll send shivers running down your spine and take you on a rough, wild ride.

If you're lookin' for words to live by, just remember: "Nothing lasts."

NoWorld

Fucking nova. Period. What more can I say of this fresh, multidimensional approach that draws heavily from Japanese influences? Shortly after meeting each other on the Net, NoiR, Haizumi and Yassun landed on the idea of the "NoWorld" project – a total musical experience placed within a broader sensory context designed by the artists.

NoWorld will be an experience created especially for you; an extensive braindance that will allow you to immerse yourself and better witness the entirety of the group's creativity. So... yeah, remember what I said about it being "fucking nova"? Only three artists, and they can create their own world? I cannot emphasize enough how exciting it will be to open our senses to this brilliant and seemingly inexhaustible well of creativity at their disposal. NoiR, Haizumi and Yassun have my full attention. The premiere is already marked on my calendar. I'll give you a minute to mark it on yours right now...

The song "Do or Die", which you can hear by tuning in to us, will get your blood pumping, and it's only a tiny taste of the larger experience they will soon unveil. Their braindance project aims to redefine our physical and emotional connection with music. If you have any time off from work stowed away, now's the time to burn it. Don't expect a 50-minute album you can turn on for the commute home – this will be a full-body, multi-hour journey. If this one track is any indication, you're gonna want to disappear from the world for a whole day... and enter NoWorld.

text:
Top 13

Home

Hotline

Entolim

Entolim is a solo artist from Dogtown. Imagine that for a moment, if you can. You're mid-thought, composing a song, then you hear Colonel Asshole blast a message over the zone's loudspeakers. Or you feel a BARGHEST convoy shake the walls as it drives past. I know, I know... Night City is no utopia either. But at least our lives and creative processes aren't interrupted by the constant threat of losing electricity, or running water, or any other basic need. But, through community, life finds a way! I admit I was touched when I heard how even the little things could make such an impact: a small power generator here, a little soundproofing there, some help with wiring, even just a kind word. A neighbor might invite you over to use the table where he cleans old processors for sale at the stadium's black market, so you can at least write your music with a functional lamp over head. Yeah, the situation might be shit, but even small lights can shine through the dark.

It's this theme of connectedness that resonates the most for me with Entolim's "LIT". On the surface, the rhythm might feel a bit trance, but underneath it beats with a togetherness. We're all going somewhere, and we're all going together, there's no denying it. Nobody is alone. We are, all of us, one big network that wants the same thing. Hell, I don't know, there's layers here, is what I'm trying to say. Maybe you'll feel the same ones I did.

To wrap up, here's a few words from Entolim himself:

“To enjoy life, you need to find balance and understand what moves you.”

text:
Top 13

Home

Hotline

Skin on Flesh

The cultural collab brought to the world by Laura Jiménez Alvarez (vocals, lyrics) and Michiel Sybers (composition, bass, guitars) delivers big on energy. The feeling that they motivate and inspire each other seems baked into every note.

How many of you have ever had to search for your tribe? A place to belong? Maybe after Night City chewed you up and spat you out? Have you pretended to be someone else just to fit in? I get it, 'cause let's be real, you can't face this city alone.

When Laura came to Night City and tried to find a place with the Valentinos, she realized she didn't have the grit they were looking for. Rather than force herself into a mold that didn't fit, she looked for a new home. That's when the Mox opened their arms.

Michi, on the other hand, immigrated here after a flood destroyed his home in Belgium. Night City flows at its own speed and he dove right in, taking merc contracts on the side to get by. Without any close chooms, he spent his free time alone with his guitar and a few substances I won't mention by name (nothing to see here, NCPD).

The story goes, Laura and Michi met at a party that turned to disaster. Now, I'm no a psychologist, but as an NC native, I know how strong crisis bonding can be.

Tune in to hear their song "El Tiempo", which is about escaping an emotional cage of your own making. When you're struggling, know that you're not alone. When you lower your defenses, know that you open yourself to something human and altogether lacking in today's world: understanding, acceptance and love.

While I stop crying, here's a message straight from Skin on Flesh:

"We all stumble, but it's up to you how to learn from it and keep moving. Follow your heart and always stay true to yourself."

Frost, Justtjokay, Dubbygotbars, Knyvez

Justtjokay, Frost, Knyvez and Dubbygotbars have arrived on Growl FM with their new song "Killshot", but you might recognize their names already from the Net or the media. A few months back they leaked NCPD data on the fight against scavs and the illegal cyberware trade (it... wasn't good). The NCPD later tried to doctor said data and claimed: "We're working super hard! No one loves public safety and hates scavs more than us! Just look at the REAL data!” (I'm paraphrasing.) You stay classy, NCPD. Besides dropping a hot, new track, these four self-taught netrunners are dropping truth bombs all over the city. If they hope to keep a lid on other statistical nightmares, the NCPD should consider upgrading their ICE... What do y'all think – are NC badges doing their best to squash the scavs and their black market deals? Maybe they could use a hand to monitor the crisis from some savvy netrunners... wink wink, nudge nudge.

But let's step out of the Net for a sec and get back to the music scene. This group features Justtjokay and Dubbygotbars on vocals, with Frost and Knyvez as producers. And let me tell you... the song's title – "Killshot" – is an understatement. This this is a nuclear warhead. It's a perfect representation of their ties to Heywood. You can feel the street in every beat. It's about rebellion, oppression and a deep, collective anxiety that's as bottomless as the mimosas at a preemo brunch spot. It's about tension waiting for its release – the calm before a massive shitstorm.

As dark as that sounds, the group has an uplifiting message to share with all you current and future fans:

“It sounds cliché, but as long as you work hard, trust the process and follow what you believe in, your efforts will be rewarded.”

text:
Top 13

Home

Hotline

Haru Nemuri

Haru Nemuri is a composer, performer and anarchist close to my heart. She's a triple threat!

Little is known about her aside from rumor. Personlly, that mystery is part of the appeal. According to one rumor, she once blew up the car of Biotechnica department head responsible for knowingly spraying a corn field with a pesticide unsafe safe for humans. The field workers were not given masks. Word is she may have also been the mastermind behind the netrunner raid on Raven Microcybernetics after they refused to pay damages to employees who were injured by an explosion on one of the corp's production lines. As for rumor number three, she may be heir to the Kenjiri Technology fortune following the merger with Kiroshi.

As badly as I want these stories to be true, they just don't shout Haru Nemuri. Dig into just a fraction of her lyrics and you'll know she's not the type to plant bombs and organize raids. Haru Nemuri wants to draw our attention to the disconnect between the human soul and the world's expectations of us. In her song "Samayoeru mama yuke", she sings about wanting to die for something beautiful. Not through violence, but through self-sacrifice. About finding purpose in a world where your power to act was taken from you. It's strong stuff – just not strong in the way the rumors paint it.

The gap between Haru Nemuri's legends and her lyrics has given fans space to think and interpret as they wish. Maybe she's inspired some people to fight back in the literal sense, but I get the feeling that's not what she's calling for. Rather, she wants to remind us of our human side as we endure the lopsided struggles in our society – so we don't lose who we are.

I'll finish the thought with one of her quotes:

"Don't forget that you always have an alternative."

text:
Top 13

Home

Hotline

Kiba

Legend says Kiba hasn't gotten up from his netrunner chair in three years, and he uses a doll whenever he needs to make an appearance in person. Why? There are two versions: either he's holed up at a Tyger Claws den because he fears for his life on the streets, or the Tygers are holding him prisoner because he crossed them. The truth is anyone's guess.

Before he disappeared, Kiba was a regular sight in Night City clubs, who'd built quite the rep as a DJ. He also often played raves at the Nicte Collective, usually incorporating a visual component that based on recordings of night drives in Seattle. This is the kind of trance that keeps you vibin' all night.

Despite being MIA, Kiba is officially back with new music. No concert dates yet, though - sorry, chooms. Fingers crossed he jacks out  of the Net for at least a night – wherever he performs that next set is gonna be e-lect-tric. Although who's to say it'll be the same Kiba? It has been three years...

Kiba's latest track “Slipstream” (tune in for a listen) definitely carries an energy that shows Kiba's evolution as an artist. I don't need a braindance for that iconic voice to transport me straight to a training simulation. The tension he can instill in his music makes my hair stand on end. My dream: Kiba crafts a new set that starts by building that same deep-rooted anxiety then releases it through blissful catharsis. I think we could all use a little of that right now. Who's with me?

For now, Kiba has released a statement for his fans:

“Traverse the unknown.”

If anyone's selling tickets for a mind-bending journey with Kiba, I'll take twenty.  And may this new track herald his return to the music scene for a good, long time!

text:
Top 13

Home

Hotline

Aleyna Moon, Shrinjay Ghosh

I could go the traditional route with something like "A duo where two completely different worlds collide"... but let's be real, we're talking about a collaboration between a former teen idol and - I shit you not - a real-life chimpanzee.

Aleyna Moon is a SoCal native of Korean descent who was launched into dazzling stardom at just thirteen years old. We all know what happens when you drag young, impressionable kids with money-grubbing parents into showbiz and stuff their heads with all kinds of dreams and promises - they become eddy-making machines. With characteristic foresight, the studio knew at some point Aleyna would burn out and chromed her to the gills - just not on the outside. Can you imagine the controversy? So she remained poster-perfect image of wide-eyed adolescence. It turned out she could handle more than anyone expected and with a goddamn smile on her face to boot - a win-win for both sides.

When her seven-year contract was finally up, during the last concert of her tour she exposed her cybermodification and performed a few of her greatest hits with altered lyrics that were pretty unequivocal about her life under the studio's shadow for all those years. The concert lasted only twenty-one minutes before Aleyna Moon was escorted off the stage by her panicked parents and a few goons.

Now, Aleyna produces her own songs, plays some gigs remotely as a holo-projection, but otherwise keeps out of the spotlight. Musically, she's reorienting her sound to better capture that winding path between humanity and chrome as a way to spread awareness about the mental health of people have gone through heavy cybermodificaiton, whatever their reasons.

Shrinjay Ghosh, the other half of this duo, is a victim of illegal smuggling around the time of the Unification War. As some of you likely know, just about anything and everything that could cross those borders... did. Even a chimpanzee.

Yes, let's address the elephant in the room. Shrinjay is a chimp. He escaped from a cargo transport when Orbital Air got into a firefight with Tyger Claw gangoons. Once the dust settled, ultimately, it was the Tyger claws who took him in. The Tygers' boss even began to treat him like family. Over the years, he invested in neural upgrades for Shrinjay, which expanded his capacity to understand humans. In time, he learned to read, write and even speak (what?!). Of all the human culture he was exposed to however, one they drew him in the most – music. The Tyger Claw boss owned a massive vinyl collection that Shrinjay had playing on repeat. And when music plays a role in shaping one's development, eventually they're gonna want to try their own hand at it too, right? He first entered the music scene by creating and posting video content on the Net under the name Shrinjay Ghosh, apparently borrowed from one of his favorite artist's from the 2020s.

Given the incredible pasts of both Aleyna and Shrinjay, it would have been a crime against music for them NOT to work together. blocks.name: author_bio
blocks.text:
I could go the traditional route with something like "A duo where two completely different worlds collide"... but let's be real, we're talking about a collaboration between a former teen idol and - I shit you not - a real-life chimpanzee.

Aleyna Moon is a SoCal native of Korean descent who was launched into dazzling stardom at just thirteen years old. We all know what happens when you drag young, impressionable kids with money-grubbing parents into showbiz and stuff their heads with all kinds of dreams and promises - they become eddy-making machines. With characteristic foresight, the studio knew at some point Aleyna would burn out and chromed her to the gills - just not on the outside. Can you imagine the controversy? So she remained poster-perfect image of wide-eyed adolescence. It turned out she could handle more than anyone expected and with a goddamn smile on her face to boot - a win-win for both sides.

When her seven-year contract was finally up, during the last concert of her tour she exposed her cybermodification and performed a few of her greatest hits with altered lyrics that were pretty unequivocal about her life under the studio's shadow for all those years. The concert lasted only twenty-one minutes before Aleyna Moon was escorted off the stage by her panicked parents and a few goons.

Now, Aleyna produces her own songs, plays some gigs remotely as a holo-projection, but otherwise keeps out of the spotlight. Musically, she's reorienting her sound to better capture that winding path between humanity and chrome as a way to spread awareness about the mental health of people have gone through heavy cybermodificaiton, whatever their reasons.

Shrinjay Ghosh, the other half of this duo, is a victim of illegal smuggling around the time of the Unification War. As some of you likely know, just about anything and everything that could cross those borders... did. Even a chimpanzee.

Yes, let's address the elephant in the room. Shrinjay is a chimp. He escaped from a cargo transport when Orbital Air got into a firefight with Tyger Claw gangoons. Once the dust settled, ultimately, it was the Tyger claws who took him in. The Tygers' boss even began to treat him like family. Over the years, he invested in neural upgrades for Shrinjay, which expanded his capacity to understand humans. In time, he learned to read, write and even speak (what?!). Of all the human culture he was exposed to however, one they drew him in the most – music. The Tyger Claw boss owned a massive vinyl collection that Shrinjay had playing on repeat. And when music plays a role in shaping one's development, eventually they're gonna want to try their own hand at it too, right? He first entered the music scene by creating and posting video content on the Net under the name Shrinjay Ghosh, apparently borrowed from one of his favorite artist's from the 2020s.

Given the incredible pasts of both Aleyna and Shrinjay, it would have been a crime against music for them NOT to work together. Their track "FUMES", is full of contagious energy, but with an underlying sadness and misplaced (but necessary!) optimism. After all, these two don't believe in giving up. text:

Home

Hotline

D.O.H.

D.O.H. rode with the Aldecaldos for a couple years before permanently returning to Night City. He came back for his sister, who fell on hard times. She worked netrunner security at a political office downtown. During a fundraiser, she was disguised as a hostess, watching for trespassing and suspicious activity by guests and event staff. At the end of the event, she was attacked by someone posing as a guest. The whole matter was swept under the rug, but it left her injured, intimidated and, ultimately, out of a job. That is, utnil the Mox took her under their wing.

D.O.H returned to town to reconnect with his sister after the incident. The Aldecaldos had become family, but that didn't mean his sister wasn't. Currently both of them are with the Mox and together, like unofficial private detectives, they investigate violent aggressors the NCPD and corps won't touch. Now immersed in and overwhelmed by all the unsavory shit that runs rampant in Night City, D.O.H. has turned to music as a way to vent and express himself. As a result, his sound captures an underlying tension and danger – a feeling of sinking deeper and deeper. As dark as it can be, the artist embraces his investigative work as a source of his creativity. (Un)fortunately, in Night City, this well of inspiration will never run dry.

In D.O.H.'s track "Look through my Kiroshis", it feels like the city is a living, swarming mass; a labyrinth you belong to but also one that wants to devour you. It's a moving train – if you try to hop off, it's the end of the line. You have to fight to keep moving and not get swallowed whole. Sounds familiar, doesn't it? D.O.H. knows how to extract the essence of everyday life and inject it into our earholes in a way you've probably never experienced before.

Worried you're missing a deeper meaning in his music? Or maybe you're just feeling crushed by the oppressive weight of everything everywhere all the time? If either is true, check out this message from the artist himself:

“Don't think too hard. Not everything has to be complicated.”

text:

St. Aurora

Wraith-rock. Can we call that a genre? 'Cause for St. Aurora, a group that rides with the Wraiths, I can't think of another more fitting. I didn't ask why they were excommunicated from whatever nomad nation they belonged to before. To be honest, I'm not sure I wanna know. But if that's an itch you need scratched, dear readers, catch 'em after a concert and ask 'em for all the gory details yourself. Still, it might be a touchy subject, so I wouldn't pry too deeply if I were in your shoes. Nomad-Wraith relations are far from civil, and you won't want to give the wrong impression.

St. Aurora is a group of five: Nile (vocals), Osku (guitars and vocals), Petja (guitars), Eemi (bass and vocals) and Vallu (drums and vocals). How these guys wound up in the Badlands together is anyone's guess, although I do have a few of my own. They lost their way... They went down a dark path... They took the low road... Yeah, you get the joke. ;) But a mysterious past means it's up to you, the fans! Send me all the fanfic!

I mentioned Wraith-rock, but in truth St. Aurora explores a range of genres. A dash of classic rock, a teaspoon of nu-metal, a pinch of punk, all topped with some death-metal sprinkles. It's a complex flavor that goes down smooth as gravy. Want proof? Check out their track "Going to Heaven" on Growl FM!

The inspiration for the song is about being different. If you have to change who you are to reach your destination, is it really worth going at all? The members of St. Aurora certainly don't think so. Given the context of their life as exiles, the theme makes a whole lotta sense and has given me much to think about. Who knows what other morsels about their stranger-than-fiction lives they'll toss us with the next track? I can't wait!

But before you get back to whatever it was you were (or weren't) doing, consider these words of wisdom from Nile:

“Get bored. Nothing is ever created if we don't."

ESAI, Pure 100%

Little is known about these artists. Both have confirmed that they once held high positions within Arasaka, but all details beyond that remain pure speculation. Word is they may have been part of Arasaka's aggressive share-trading strategies, and possibly even involved in the sudden collapse of MagniChromics Inc. The artists declined to comment on this particular subject.

Most of us plebs will never set foot inside an Arasaka company party, but I think we can all imagine the conversations that take place. Stock prices, the weather, stock prices again, taste in music... For this duo, the latter topic evolved well past small talk as they gushed and bonded over their favorite DJs. From that moment, they became fast friends and explored the city together in search of inspiration at all manner of dive bars and night clubs. So often did they go out, the staff at the Ho-oh club even kept a table set aside, always ready and waiting, just for them.

So how did these two former suits make the jump from discussing music to making it? Why, with the Tyger Claws' help! No, they didn't gain popularity with gang money or bribes or extortion or [insert any other crime here]. It was inspiration. The music and energy of Tyger Claw clubs suited their style best, and heavily colored their own work. By combining this club style with other influences from their cultural roots, they spun a new sound all their own.  From aggressive corporate takeovers to some of the chillest sounds you'll soak in this year. Much like how they dropped their corporate day jobs for a life at the clubs, their track "Nebula" invites listeners to disconnect from the world and just be in the moment. Unplug your brain, and plug in ESAI, Pure 100%.

Here's a little message straight from the artists:

"Live with passion! Never stop learning! And to our former Arasaka colleagues, please let us know if you manage to solve the Riemann hypothesis without us! We must know!"

text:

Thai McGrath (ft. JustCosplaySings)

A duo from Heywood that can trace their beginnings to braindances. I don't even know if these are still on the market, but I remember reliving two of them myself at a Mox club. Oh my god were they beautiful. One had this sense gentleness and charm, but also brimming with pure joy. A rare feeling these days, isn't it, chooms? The second BD, on the other hand, had me totally freaked me out and squeezing the stuffing out of my armrests. I was a nervous wreck for the rest of the evening. It gave this crushing depressive power that was colored with horror elements. These two BDs were total opposite experiences.

But when Thai (vocals, composition) and Viv (vocals, lyrics) started dabbling with their own music for these scrolls, it turned out that the music totally absorbed them, giving more of a sense satisfaction and completeness than the 'dances in their entirety ever did. (Jealous. I could use a little of that in my life right now.)

Thai McGrath and JustCosplaySings have that elusive something that gets your blood pumping just a little bit faster. Keep an eye on this pair, because have an uncanny talent for capturing emotions, feelings and even states of mind, like a freeze frame of someone's real lived experience. I guess they learned the magic to pull that off from their time tuning BDs. And, choom, their sound will stick with you. You know those spikey little seeds that stick to your clothes when you walk through a shrub? Yeah, their music's like that, except in your brain. You'll keep coming back to that emotional state that they captured in their track, like you're looking through a window directly into their minds all over again. 100% certified nova.

Did you read all of that twice and you're still confused? Just listen to "Afterlife" and you'll know what I mean. There is some heat, some romance, some tragedy. Imagine: the Mox and the Tyger Claws, timid looks and tragic desire... I'm there, I can see it! Against the world, they die – but they die as legends. So hey! If anyone at the Afterlife club sees this, it's time to name a new cocktail!

And to all our Growl FM listeners, here's a few words of wisdom straight from the mouths of Thai McGrath and JustCosplaySings:

"Take chances like there is no tomorrow. Be better than you were yesterday. Live life fully every day."

Preach! Dunno, might get that tattooed on me later.

For fans

Rockerboy. Star. Charismatic guitarist and vocalist. A legend.

Kerry Eurodyne is this era's undisputed king of REAL rock. Adored by his fans, praised by his critics, respected by his rivals. For years he's been riding a wave of popularity, resulting in instantly sold out concerts and record-breaking plays of his songs.

His career started in the underground punk band Samurai, until, he says, "One day I just decided to grow up," beginning his journey to true fame. Kerry went solo. The rest is history, filled with explosive sounds, unforgettable lyrics, Richter-scale breaking stadium concert and countless hits.

Kerry Eurodyne's career soared under the wings of MSM. From the moment he signed, thus began the Golden Age of Kerry Eurodyne – month after month of topping the charts with hit singles like "Holdin' On" or "Scream and Whisper," perfectly choreographed, spectacular concert tours (how could anyone forget the "chrome" zeppelins in Memphis!) and unprecedented artistic heights reached.

The Rockerboy lives in his beloved Night City and is currently working on his latest album, brought to you soon by MSM.

title: KERRY EURODYNE
text:
KERRY EURODYNE

Official site

Bio

Discography

Concert tour

For fans

MSM proudly presents the musical triumphs of KERRY EURODYNE!

From his debut album, "False Terrorist" to the mystical "Aether," the hit "Spiral Distortion" and the surprisingly conceptual "Persuasion of the Undecided," all the way to the controversial "Second Conflict" – Kerry Eurodyne's music is a masterpiece of rock, with uncompromising lyrics, sounds and ideas that brings everyone together, no matter their ideological or spiritual creed – a one-size fits all.

"Kerry Eurodyne is one of the last crazy prophets of rock. His songs are savage, his lyrics provocative. In an era where everything has become a copy of a copy of a copy, Eurodyne remains one-of-a-kind." Ted Hunst

"This isn't music for teeny-boppers. Eurodyne makes music for people whose veins flow with real rock 'n' roll." – Moira S. Ritz

"Persuasion of the Undecided" is a masterpiece. Period. Every time I listen to that album, I uncover new layers of meaning. It could even be the pinnacle of Kerry Eurodyne's artistic achievement. It's a story – painted in brutal brushstrokes and chrome noise – of a country that has faded out of existence before our own eyes. It's about freedom, whose taste evaporates from our lips like a distant memory. It's about a man who gives up his old life to pursue his ideals, only to discover they were all lies" – "Antimusic Magazine"

"An album about hopelessness? A lullaby for those on the verge of suicide? Or maybe a subtle joke about a Rockerboy too edgy for his time? The problem with a clear-cut interpretation of "Aether" is paradoxically also the record's greatest strength – until now fans on the Net have been debating what kind of story this album is telling. An artist couldn't dream of anything more. Hats off, Eurodyne, you'll always be our Prince of the Aether." – Hannah Icona

"Second Conflict" is clearly inspired by events from the rockerboy's life, like every record ever made. But here the references to the corporate wars and the brief, tumultuous friendship with Johnny Silverhand is Eurodyne at his most confessional – his nightmares and failed dreams laid bare for all of us. Hit play and indulge yourself in a cathartic, macabre listening experience of a lifetime." – Duane Foss

text:
Cytech

In an age of gargantuan megacorporations, it's easy to ignore the little details. You could buy a cyberarm from a company that makes a hundred different other implants... but why? Can manufacturers of limbs, muscle weaves, biomonitors and reflex boosters make just ONE truly innovative, high-quality product?

The answer's no.

That's why we created Cytech. We have a duty to detail and our working motto is, "If you try to be good at everything, you'll never be great at anything." Take our very own cyberhands: the three, four and six digit models feel as natural as a classic, organic hand. How about two digits? Extended finger length? We've got you covered. With Cytech, your hands will do things you've never imagined.

title: Nibiru-234
text:
Nibiru-234

Will YOU conquer humanity's last frontier?

Has anyone ever told you to reach for the stars? What if we said you could set foot where no human has set foot before – see the Earth as a blue dot? Not everyone has the guts.

What about you?

Utopian Inc. is seeking ambitious individuals to settle Nibiru-234 – a brand-new colony in the vicinity of Mars. This vast compound awaits volunteers to occupy its housing units, relax in its entertainment-recreation centers and pluck the fruits of its luscious gardens. Jobs are available for all settlers. We are especially seeking:
·   Scientists (astrophysicists, radio astronomers, geologists, etc.)
·   Ripperdocs
·   Technicians
·   Off-world mining specialists
·   Manual laborers
Let your Earthly worries go and start afresh! Be the person you've always wanted to be! Nibiru-234 is the answer you've been waiting for.

REGISTRATION HAS ENDED. THANK YOU FOR APPLYING.

title: NETdir://fullbodyconversion.web
text:
The Soviet Center for Conversion is a facility that offers safe and reliable FBCs (Full Body Conversions). Every year we carry out close to 250 such procedures. It is our privilege to make the great achievements of soviet science available to all citizens of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics and foreigners (with exceptions), regardless of one's state of health.

Where are FBC procedures conducted? Located in Abakan in Siberia, the Soviet Center for Conversion is directed by Dr. Boris Borisovich Federov, whose knowledge and experience defies ordinary praise. He is best known for outfitting over a thousand miners at once for labor in harsh conditions.

How to pay for a FBC? You have two options. The first consists of signing up for our FBC waiting list and pledging to carry out manual labor in a Siberian mine. Applications will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.
The second option consists of cash payment (in Soviet rubles).
Please note that FBC procedures conducted within the USSR are less expensive than in Japan or the former USA. Why? Soviet technology is much more advanced, with proven ripperdoc facilities operating around the clock at the SCC in Abakan.

title: NETdir://darkstar.web/mr_kipper
text:
Home

Mr. Kipper

Private Press

Our Top Bangers

Mr. Kipper, Man of Mystery

The multi-talented and notoriously enigmatic Mr. Kipper likely enjoys more fame than any other Highrider on Earth. Although he rarely gives interviews and his identity is a greater mystery than the fate of Garry the Prophet, tickets for the artist's terranean tour are already sold out. If you're not among the lucky few to catch Mr. Kipper live, Dark Star has you covered with two of his latest singles: "Choke Hold" and "Rolla".

"Choke Hold" and "Rolla" may surprise even the most loyal Mr. Kipper fans. Th lyrics written and rapped by the artist himself are an added chef's kiss to his already lauded work. Does Mr. Kipper defy genre classificaiton as we recognize it today? Is it possible to tell when he's experimenting rather than keeping to a familiar musical orbit? It's no secret that Mr. Kipper likes to keep us guessing – the only mystery is where he will find his next inspiration.

If you want Mr. Kipper flooding your ear canals 24/7, tune into our new radio station: 99.9 Impulse. Whether you're drifting on solar winds to the far reaches of the cosmos or you're washing your dishes, do it all to the original rhythms composed by your favorite Highrider.

Mr. Kipper

Private Press

Our Top Bangers

Private Press: From the Stars to Stardom

Brocki and Wóycicki, Wóycicki and Brocki – suitably out-of-this-world names for the cosmic DJ duo Private Press. Their star is shining brighter than ever right now. These mysterious Highriders are newcomers from a musical scene in orbit that is currently on the rise (or rather descent?) as their sound invades ever more earholes and hearts of us Earthlings!

From Grobel Orbital Station to Night City – Private Press is set to perform at club Riot! Tickets for the 99.9 Impulse promo tour are already selling out at the speed of light. The star of the evening will be Mr. Kipper who, in collaboration with Private Press, has created an exclusive set for a new terrestrial radio station.

"Music that transcends all space" – this is the message that resounds in every beat produced by Wóycicki and Brocki. As citizens of the universe, the members of Private Press draw inspiration from both Highrider and "Groundsider" culture. That explains how their music seems to resonate with everyone. It's a sound that bypasses your brain and flows straight into your heart and feet. Wanna hear it for youself? Come see Private Press and Mr. Kipper – the greatest collab the solar system has ever seen – only at Riot!
